repairs.source_context: Notation says bounded approximation operator; paragraph before retained identity says Q:X->X bounded. Linearity is not explicit. The retained identity itself does not need linearity, but the estimated-packet identity does.
repairs.counterexample: X=R, Q(x)=|x|, s=1, j=-1, jhat=0. Q is norm bounded by 1. f-fhat=0 while (I-Q)s+(I-Q)(j-jhat)=-2.
repairs.repair: State that every Q_m used in estimated-packet reconstruction is a bounded linear operator. Add linear to notation and relevant theorem hypotheses.
repairs.repaired_argument: Linearity gives Q_m(s+j-jhat)=Q_ms+Q_m(j-jhat). Triangle inequality and the linear operator norm give the advertised bound.

repairs.kind: actual false claim if constants unconstrained
repairs.source_context: Local displayed inequalities impose no nonnegativity on A_v, B_v. The induction multiplies by child lower constants.
repairs.counterexample: Two successive zero maps on R along a root to child to terminal unary tree, both with A_v=-1 and B_v=0. Each local inequality -|x|^2<=0<=0 holds. Recursive lower constant at root is (-1)(-1)=1, but leaf output is zero for x=1.
repairs.repair: Require 0<=A_v<=B_v<infinity. Strict A_v>0 is needed only when asserting a positive frame lower bound.
repairs.repaired_argument: All child a(w) are nonnegative by induction, so multiplying local lower bounds preserves inequalities. Upper constants are nonnegative as well.
impact: nonunitary recursive bounds only; unitary pruning and additive optimization unaffected

repairs.source_context: Earlier H_tau=1_[tau,1]. Haar subsection moves to R or a chosen extension but does not prescribe the endpoint continuation.
repairs.counterexample: Use earlier bounded-interval step H_{1/4}=1_[1/4,1], amplitude 1, shifted Haar support [1/2,3/2] of length 1, positive on [1/2,1], negative on [1,3/2]. The coefficient is 1/2 despite the support not crossing tau. The extra discontinuity at 1 is responsible.
repairs.repair: In the Haar subsections explicitly use H_tau(t)=1_[tau,infinity)(t) on R. Its restriction to (0,1) agrees with the earlier step. Any endpoint extension must use the declared half-line model on the analyzed supports.
repairs.repaired_argument: Each half-line step is constant on a support excluding its sole jump; direct integration produces the triangular coefficient. The half-cell shift chooses a support at distance at least L/4 from its endpoints. L below minimum separation excludes other jumps.
impact: two-grid detection; no claim of deduplicated recovery or synthesis for the redundant system

repairs.source_context: Definition of linear tube bound supplies the estimate only for 0 < delta < delta0; theorem does not repeat that range.
repairs.counterexample: For the unit circle in R^2, mu(N_delta)=4 pi delta for 0 < delta < 1. Thus C=4 pi,delta0 = 1 qualifies. With E=unit disk, F=disk of radius 3.9, delta=3, E triangle F is inside N_3 but its area 14.21 pi exceeds C delta = 12 pi.
repairs.repair: Require 0 < delta < delta0, where delta0 is the radius in the linear tube bound.
repairs.repaired_argument: Symmetric-difference inclusion then invokes the available tube estimate in its stated range, followed by exact scalar region formula.
impact: geometric mask bound; boundary-band corollary already says small delta

repairs.source_context: The section supplies independent centered sub-Gaussian noises and the earlier fixed jump model. Final sentence says packet error converges to zero without a mode.
repairs.repair: Say convergence in probability in every finite L^p norm, for the fixed finite model and admissible sampling grids above. Do not claim almost sure convergence.
repairs.repaired_argument: For each tolerance e > 0 and confidence delta > 0 the deterministic bound on the good event is eventually below e. Hence limsup P(error>e)<=delta. Delta is arbitrary.

repairs.source_context: Recovery section already assumes a Lipschitz background, no jump on a sample, at most one per cell. The minimum amplitude is defined only for a nonempty jump list.
repairs.counterexample: Tau=1/2 lies on samples for every evenn. Thus an asymptotic assertion over all integern cannot silently use the no-jump-on-grid assumption.
repairs.repair: State Q>=1 when defining min amplitude;Q=0 is trivial if handled separately. In asymptotic statements explicitly retain fixed nonzero amplitudes, finite Q, positive separation and admissible grids.
repairs.repaired_argument: On those grids, separation eventually gives at most one jump per cell and the original threshold proof applies.
impact: clarifies inherited asymptotic domain; no threshold constant changed

repairs.source_context: Finite packet-tree context is explicit. Original recursion only specifies strict comparison branches. g>0 tacitly presupposes a competitor.
repairs.counterexample: A one-node tree has no second smallest pruning cost. Equal stop and split costs leave both strict reconstruction branches unspecified.
repairs.repair: Retain on ties using c(v)<=sum child F; split otherwise. Require a competing pruning for gap definition, or state singleton trivially stable. Define g = min_{L!=L*}(C(L)-C(L*)).
repairs.repaired_argument: Either tie choice attains the displayed minimum; stop-on-ties makes the algorithm total. For competitors, each gap decreases by at most 2epsilon_star.
impact: selection rule completeness, no alteration of optimal cost formula

repairs.source_context: Sub-Gaussian subsection already assumes independent noises across sample sites. Repeated-measurements corollary adds independent repetitions.
repairs.repair: Optionally make all site and repetition noises independent explicit. This is a clarification of inherited context, not an identified contradiction.
repairs.repaired_argument: Averages at separate sites remain independent with variance proxy sigma^2/R; adjacent differences have proxy 2 sigma^2/R.

repairs.source_context: Section explicitly operates in relevant polyphase spaces, so z^{-d} is a channel delay. Text calls it input delay without units.
repairs.counterexample: N=2 and scalar multiplierz^{-1} on both channels produces a two-fine-sample shift, not a one-fine-sample shift.
repairs.repair: Specify d coarse-channel samples; this corresponds to N d fine samples in the N-phase one-dimensional setting.
repairs.repaired_argument: Inverse channel transform shifts each channel by d, and interleaving multiplies the fine-address offset by N.
impact: interpretation of reconstruction delay, no matrix identity changed

repairs.source_context: Statement says isolated jump without a local regularity class; proof is citation only.
repairs.repair: Restrict contextual Gibbs statement to a periodic piecewise C1 function with an isolated nonzero jump. Keep explicitly outside proved-result/Lean denominator. Authenticate an exact source separately if claiming fresh literature verification.
repairs.repaired_argument: Standard classical Gibbs asymptotics apply under this regularity; retained-packet theorems themselves only use the exact algebraic error identity and do not depend on this fact.
impact: contextual imported fact only; no downstream proof dependency

repairs.source_context: The stated moment-generating-function proxy permits sigma=0, but the displayed tail proof divides by sigma^2.
repairs.counterexample: The stated proof expression is undefined at sigma=0. The theorem itself remains valid.
repairs.repair: Handle sigma=0 separately: a 0-sub-Gaussian centered variable is zero almost surely, so the deterministic contrast bound applies with zero noise; thereafter assume sigma>0 for the Chernoff division.
repairs.repaired_argument: For sigma=0, Markov gives P(eta>=t)<=exp(-lambda t) for every lambda > 0 and t > 0; let lambda tend to infinity and repeat for -eta.
impact: probability proof boundary case; recovery constant unchanged

repairs.kind: false prose assertion about actual noise maxima
repairs.source_context: Remark says the maximum noise contrast grows slowly with n at fixed scale. Sub-Gaussianity only supplies an upper-tail certificate, not actual growth.
repairs.counterexample: Independent Rademacher noises taking values plus/minus sigma are sigma-sub-Gaussian, while every adjacent noise contrast is bounded by 2 sigma for all n.
repairs.repair: Say the displayed uniform high-probability certificate scales like sigma*sqrt(log n), so this certificate does not yield consistency at fixed sigma. Decreasing effective noise or repeated averaging supplies sufficient regimes.
repairs.repaired_argument: This describes the bound actually proved and makes no unsupported lower-growth claim for general sub-Gaussian distributions.
impact: noise-scaling explanatory remark only; no recovery theorem invalidated

repairs.source_context: The latest 20-result core declares conjugate-linear first slot. Annals standalone does not specify that convention but its smooth-Haar proof writes an un-conjugated s-integral. On integration into a common final paper, the displayed equality must follow the common convention.
repairs.counterexample: With s(t)=i*t on [0,L] and real normalized Haar, the un-conjugated integral has the opposite sign to the inner product under a conjugate-linear first slot. Magnitudes are identical.
repairs.repair: Put a complex conjugate over s(t)-s(t+L/2) in the pairing integral, or explicitly use an equivalent consistent inner-product ordering.
repairs.repaired_argument: The modulus of the conjugated difference is unchanged, so ML^(3/2)/4 and every subsequent absolute coefficient estimate stay exactly the same.
impact: one proof equality under combined-edition conventions; no numerical threshold or theorem conclusion changed

critical_derivations.higher_order_trace: For ell<m, truncated-power ell derivative is continuous at tau; for ell=m it has unit jump; for ell>m its side derivatives vanish. Packet derivative-jump matrix is diagonal in (m,tau). Subtracting coefficients cancels every trace through r - 1; piecewise integration by parts cancels interface terms, giving global W^{r,p}.
critical_derivations.higher_order_location: Integral in location of phi_{m-1,u}; its Lp norm on (0,1) is <=1/((m-1)!((m-1)p+1)^(1/p)), so Minkowski gives the displayed Lipschitz constant.
critical_derivations.geometry: Region intersections partition the domain exactly. Equal-amplitude error is |a|mu(E triangle F)^(1/p). A local tube estimate can only be applied inside its radius range.
critical_derivations.deterministic: D_k=a_q+(s(t_{k+1})-s(t_k))+(eta_{k+1}-eta_k) on a one-jump cell. Residual<=Mh+2eps. Strict threshold interval exists iff a_min>2b. Midpoint error<=h/2 and disjoint detected cells let the location Lp errors add in pth powers.
critical_derivations.probability: Independent sigma-subGaussian differences have mgf<=exp(sigma^2lambda^2). Chernoff gives two-tail<=2exp(-t^2/(4sigma^2)); n-cell union bound with t =2sigma sqrt(log(2n/delta)) gives delta. Adjacent contrasts need not be independent for the union bound. Sigma=0 is handled as deterministic zero noise, avoiding division by zero.
critical_derivations.haar: Smooth coefficient<=ML^(3/2)/4 by pairing half-cell points. Half-line step coefficient=|a|sqrtL min(u,1-u). Bounded noise coefficient<=eps sqrtL. Compare upper and lower for threshold. Modulo L, either grid places tau at distance >= L/4 from endpoints.
critical_derivations.best_basis: Finite prunings give an attained minimum; each subtree pruning stops or splits. Uniform pruning-cost perturbation<= epsilon_star implies optimum difference<= epsilon_star. Strict competitor gaps remain positive if 2 epsilon_star < g. Ties/singletons need explicit total selection conventions.
critical_derivations.difference: Binomial coefficients have sum of absolute values 2^m; (d + 1)st difference vanishes on a degree<=d polynomial stencil. The breakpoint-band theorem requires a nonzero response assumption and does not prove every breakpoint has one.
